title: Midday Brief — Sat 28 Nov

stories.board: Netanyahu offers Eisenkot first turn as Israel's PM
stories.headline: Netanyahu says Eisenkot can be prime minister first in a shared deal
stories.what: Benjamin Netanyahu said he would let Gadi Eisenkot lead Israel first, with Netanyahu as his backup, in a rotation (taking turns) unity government. Eisenkot has about a week left to form a government.
stories.why: It is the first time Netanyahu has agreed to go second, and it could decide who runs Israel next.
stories.sides: Netanyahu calls it needed because of big threats to Israel; rivals Yair Golan and Yair Lapid call it a trick and say Netanyahu already lost.

stories.board: Canada's top court mostly upholds Quebec's Bill 21
stories.headline: Supreme Court lets Quebec keep most of its religious symbols ban
stories.what: On Friday, Canada's Supreme Court said Quebec can keep Bill 21, which stops some public workers like teachers from wearing religious symbols such as a kippah, hijab or cross at work. Only the face-covering rule for members of Quebec's legislature was struck down.
stories.why: It decides how far provinces can go in limiting rights by using the notwithstanding clause (a rule that lets governments override some Charter rights).
stories.sides: Quebec's government and Alberta's premier call it a win; Muslim and civil-liberties groups call it a dark day for rights. Prime Minister Carney said Ottawa will not use the notwithstanding clause itself.

quick_hits: The US military disabled another ship trying to sneak past its blockade (block on ships) of Iran's ports; the crew was not hurt (CENTCOM, Fox News).
An explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan killed 10 people, most of them children (AP).
big_picture: Big choices about who leads and what rights mean: Israel may get a new prime minister, and Canada's top court drew a new line on religious symbols.
